title: Essential Addons for Elementor <= 6.8.7 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to 'page_id' Parameter via Elementor Revision
description: The Essential Addons for Elementor – Popular Elementor Templates & Widgets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 6.8.7 via the `page_id` parameter of the `register_user()` function. The vulnerability exists because the handler's post status deny-list rejects `future`, `draft`, and `pending` but admits `inherit` — the status carried by every WordPress revision — allowing an attacker to substitute a revision ID for a live page ID, while a flawed "last saved by administrator" check reads `post_author` on revisions (which reflects the editing administrator) rather than the `_edit_last` meta that is never copied to revisions, and the nonce gate is rendered ineffective because any unauthenticated visitor can freely obtain a valid nonce via the `wp_ajax_nopriv_eael_get_token` endpoint. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register an account with a role as high as Editor — gaining capabilities including `edit_others_posts`, `publish_pages`, `upload_files`, and `unfiltered_html` — by naming a revision whose `_elementor_data` contains an elevated role an administrator previously saved and later reverted on a page bearing the Login/Register widget. Successful exploitation requires that the site has "Anyone can register" enabled and that an administrator has at some point saved and then reverted a non-default "New User Role" on an affected page.
cwe: CWE-269 CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management

title: WPSpeed <= 2.6.10 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via User Nickname/Display Name

This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read full authenticated WooCommerce REST product records for any published product — including private underscore-prefixed meta, purchase notes, downloadable file URLs for paid digital products, catalog-hidden products, and edit-context representations — across the `/wc/v1`, `/wc/v2`, `/wc/v3`, and `/wc-analytics` REST namespaces. The bypass is triggered by appending a query parameter whose value contains the literal string `/dokan/mcp/` to any WooCommerce REST product endpoint (e.g., `/wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id}?x=/dokan/mcp/`); note that percent-encoding the slashes prevents the bypass, as the unencoded literal slash characters are required for the regex to match.

title: Reset Database <= 1.1.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation to Missing Capability and Nonce Check in process_reset()
description: The Reset Database plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation in versions up to, and including, 1.1.3. This is due to the process_reset() function being registered on admin_init with no capability check, a computed-but-unused nonce, a gating condition that passes whenever no WordPress administrator literally named 'admin' exists (the default on modern installs), and an identity test that verifies the ATTACKER'S OWN password rather than an administrator's. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The public Manage Preferences page issues a nonce to unauthenticated visitors, meaning there is no effective authorization barrier — an unauthenticated attacker can store the malicious payload as their first_name and have it executed the next time any newsletter is sent by the site operator. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

title: UsersWP <= 1.2.78 - Unauthenticated Account Access via Predictable Dummy User Password Disclosed through Registration Form Hash
description: The UsersWP – Front-end login form, User Registration, User Profile & Members Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized account access via Use of Predictable Password in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.78 The vulnerability exists because `get_dummy_user_passowrd()` derives the shared password for all 25 built-in dummy user accounts as the first 15 characters of `substr(hash('SHA256', AUTH_KEY . site_url()), 0, 25)`, while the full 25-character value of that same hash is simultaneously embedded in the hidden `uwp_register_hash` field rendered on every registration form response — reachable without authentication via both the public `/register/` page and the `wp_ajax_nopriv_uwp_ajax_register_form` AJAX handler, even when user registration is disabled. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover the dummy user password directly from a single HTTP request and use it to authenticate as any of the 25 built-in dummy accounts (such as antawn, chynna, or kiki) through `wp-login.php`, potentially achieving privilege escalation if any dummy account holds an elevated role. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously created dummy users via the plugin's Tools page.

title: Easy Digital Downloads <= 3.7.2 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Administrator Account Takeover via Guest Checkout Email Binding at PayPal Capture
description: The Easy Digital Downloads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authentication bypass leading to administrator account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 3.7.2. During a PayPal guest checkout, the email address entered in the guest-checkout field is trusted as proof of identity: edd_get_purchase_form_user() binds the new guest order to an existing WordPress user purely on an email-address match, rewriting the order's user_id to that user's ID. The PayPal capture sink PurchaseUser::maybe_log_in_after_capture() then looked the user up by the order email (get_user_by( 'email', $order->email )) and, when $order->user_id equalled that user's ID (which the email-binding step guarantees), issued an authenticated session with wp_set_auth_cookie(). An unauthenticated attacker who starts a guest checkout using an administrator's email address (where that administrator has no existing EDD customer record) and completes the PayPal purchase flow therefore receives an authenticated session as that administrator — a full account takeover. title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Backup Restore Comment Discard SQLi
description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.
cwe: CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management

title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Database Restore Whitespace Trimming
description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.
cwe: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data

title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Large Table Backup SQLi
description: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not safely process the output of the external database dump tool when backing up large tables, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to store profile data that turns into SQL executed when an administrator later restores the backup, for example to grant themselves the administrator role.
cwe: CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management

title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Search and Replace Recursion Limit
description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .
cwe: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data

title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Search and Replace Length Corruption
description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep serialized string lengths consistent when their database search and replace processes certain serialized values, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data that becomes an attacker-chosen PHP object after an administrator runs a URL-lengthening search and replace or a migration restore.

When the replacement changes the length of the text, the declared string lengths inside the stored value no longer match and the corrupted value is written back, so when WordPress later reads it the trailing bytes are parsed as further serialized structure, including an object of a class the attacker named. No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on classes available from other installed code.
cwe: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data

title: FV Flowplayer Video Player <= 7.5.56.7212 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content

title: QODE Wishlist for WooCommerce <= 1.2.9 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'table_title' Shared Wishlist Field via Guest Cookie
description: The QODE Wishlist for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'qode_wishlist_for_woocommerce_guests_items' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by guests because the required wp_rest nonce is publicly emitted to unauthenticated visitors on the /wishlist/ page, and the attacker controls the transient key, meaning the payload is stored site-wide and only requires a victim to open a crafted share URL and click the injected title link. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

title: Customer Reviews for WooCommerce <= 5.127.0 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure in 'search' Parameter
description: The Customer Reviews for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 5.127.0 via the 'search' parameter of the cr_show_more_all_reviews and cr_show_more_reviews AJAX actions. This is due to the handlers being hooked on wp_ajax_nopriv_* without a capability check (and, in the product-page handler, with a nonce check that is behind a filter defaulting to false) while passing the visitor-supplied search string straight into get_comments() as the 'search' argument, which core expands into LIKE conditions over comment_author, comment_author_email, comment_author_url, comment_author_IP and comment_content. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract review author email addresses and IP addresses — fields WordPress and WooCommerce never expose to the public — one character at a time by observing whether the returned result set matches a probed substring.
cwe: CWE-200 CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

title: BlockArt Blocks <= 2.4.3 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Contributor+) Sensitive Information Disclosure via 'queryArgs' and 'query[post_status]' Block Attributes
description: The BlockArt Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder Blocks ,WordPress Block Plugin, Sections & Template Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the title, excerpt, and full content of other users' draft, pending, and private posts, exposing that content to unauthenticated visitors on the published permalink. This is exploitable by an Author-level user because WordPress's wp_filter_post_kses preserves block-comment JSON in HTML comments, allowing the malicious queryArgs and query[post_status] attributes to survive post saving and execute on every unauthenticated request to the published URL. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that attacker only needs to see the data themselves (not expose it to unauthenticated visitors) — satisfied by viewing their own preview URL. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.
cwe: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization

affected.product: BlockArt Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder Blocks ,WordPress Block Plugin, Sections & Template Library

title: Check & Log Email <= 2.0.17 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Moderation Email Log + ThickBox Title Attribute
description: The Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open the relevant log entry and click the planted anchor link in the Preview panel, at which point the ThickBox gadget parses the title attribute as live HTML in the wp-admin origin. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

affected.product: Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging

title: Church Admin <= 5.1.7 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'lat' Parameter
description: The Church Admin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'lat' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only exploitable when a Google Maps API key has been configured in Church Admin settings, as the vulnerable sink is only reached when that option is present.
cwe: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

title: immonex Kickstart <= 1.19.0 - Unauthenticated Local File Inclusion via 'inx-r-cidata' Parameter
description: The immonex Kickstart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 1.19.0 via the 'inx-r-cidata (JSON blob containing 'template' and 'template_folders')' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The filename-level sanitization that strips dot-slash sequences applies only to the template filename component, not to the attacker-supplied template_folders directory paths, rendering it ineffective against directory traversal via that parameter.
cwe: CWE-98 CWE-98 Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program

title: SureDash <= 1.13.0 - Authenticated (Custom+) Privilege Escalation to /suredash/v1/save-settings REST Endpoint
description: The SureDash – Community, Courses & Member Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.13.0 This is due to the `save_settings()` REST handler at `/suredash/v1/save-settings` being gated only by `admin_permission_callback()`, which authorizes any holder of the custom `manage_portal_dashboard` capability (Portal Manager role) without requiring `promote_users`, `edit_users`, or `manage_options`, combined with `sanitize_settings_data()` iterating all attacker-supplied keys with no allow-list, allowing arbitrary keys such as `default_role` to pass through `sanitize_text_field()` unchanged and be persisted into the `portal_settings` option via `update_option()` with no role-validity check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Portal Manager-level access and above to poison the `default_role` setting to `administrator`, after which any subsequent new-user registration through the publicly accessible block-register endpoint reads the corrupted setting and passes it directly to `wp_insert_user()`, producing a full WordPress Administrator account under the attacker's control. The exploit requires two steps: a POST to the authenticated `save-settings` endpoint to overwrite `default_role`, followed by triggering a new registration through the unauthenticated block-register endpoint to receive the escalated account. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

description: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. title: Nexter Blocks Pro <= 5.0.10 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Unicode Collation Confusion in 'tpgb_acf_key' Parameter
description: The Nexter Blocks Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 via the `tpgb_ajax_register_user()` function. This is due to a byte-level denylist on the `tpgb_acf_key[]` and `tpgb_acf[]` parameters that fails to block Unicode look-alike characters — such as U+1E87 and U+00E7 in a key like `ẇp_çapabilities` — whose UTF-8 byte sequences do not match any ASCII-based pattern check, while the database's default accent-insensitive collation (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) treats the decorated key as equivalent to the canonical `wp_capabilities` row, causing `update_user_meta()` to overwrite the newly registered user's role with `administrator`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register a new account bearing the full Administrator role, gaining complete control over the WordPress site including the ability to install plugins, modify files, and execute arbitrary code. The nonce required by the handler is publicly emitted on any page containing the tp-login-register block, making the full exploit chain — nonce retrieval, a single crafted registration POST, and the plugin's own `autologin` flow — trivially reachable on any default install where user registration is enabled. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.
cwe: CWE-269 CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management

title: Quick Page/Post Redirect 5.2.1 - 5.2.3 - Backdoor via Off-Repository Update Channel
description:
The Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 was distributed with a hidden update mechanism that fetched Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 updates from its author's own server instead of WordPress.org, which was used to push a backdoored build to sites, allowing the attacker controlling that server to inject arbitrary content into pages and to deliver arbitrary code to affected sites.

Version 5.2.1, as published on WordPress.org, bundled the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker library (updater/ directory) configured to poll https://anadnet.com/updates/?action=get_metadata&slug=quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4. In March 2021 that server delivered a modified 5.2.3 build, different from the 5.2.3 later published on WordPress.org, which kept the update channel and added a the_content filter that, for logged-out visitors on single posts and pages, fetched content from https://w.anadnet.com/bro/3/ (passing the site host, request URI and visitor User-Agent) and prepended the response to the post (observed serving SEO spam links to search engine crawlers). Because the version string matched a later WordPress.org release, affected sites were not offered a clean update until 5.2.4.

Indicators of compromise:
- Outbound requests to anadnet.com or w.anadnet.com
- An updater/ directory (Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker, Puc v4p10) inside wp-content/Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/
- The strings filter_the_content_in_the_main_loop, ppr_pro, QQQEND or w.anadnet.com in page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php
- page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php with MD5 ad717da18cf8a2b69899c0d7dafee05a (tampered 5.2.3)

Remediation: remove the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 (it has been closed on WordPress.org), or at minimum reinstall the clean 5.2.4 from WordPress.org, delete any leftover updater/ directory, verify the files with "wp Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 verify-checksums quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4", clear the opcode cache, and treat any site that ran the tampered build as potentially compromised.

title: Social Media Auto Poster <= 6.2.9 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Contributor+) Arbitrary Log Deletion and Disclosure via 'post' Parameter
description: The Social Media Auto Poster – Schedule & Publish to Buffer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.9. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to delete Buffer sync log history for and disclose Buffer sync log contents of arbitrary posts, including those authored by administrators. The nonce used as the sole gate is not bound to any specific post ID, so a nonce harvested from the attacker's own draft editor screen is valid against any arbitrary post ID submitted in the request.

title: PayPlus Payment Gateway <= 8.3.4 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary Order Payment Manipulation via generate-link-payment AJAX Action
description: The PayPlus Payment Gateway plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to generate PayPlus payment page links for arbitrary WooCommerce orders belonging to any customer, overwrite those orders' payment method and PayPlus-related order meta, and trigger PayPlus API calls using the store's credentials — including, when a POS EMV device is configured, initiating a charge request to the store's physical POS terminal. The exploit requires no nonce and no special capability beyond being logged in, as the authorization block is unreachable on the AJAX path due to the inverted isset() predicate.
